CST Official Help | 3D common preloadedmacro common preloadedmacro tdr from s parameter
Time Signal Processing / TDR from S-parameter

P ost-Processing: Tools > Result Templates

This result templates calculates time domain reflectometry (TDR) results from S-parameters. The required input time domain signals are determined by the specified frequency domain filter (see below) and the output signals are obtained from this filter and the given S-parameters by means of a Fourier transform. Refer to the general introduction of the TDR computation for more theoretical details.

Specify Port/Mode [3D Simulation] or Specify Task/Port [Circuits & Systems] frame

Defines the S-parameters used for the TDR calculation.

Time domain sampling options frame

t_end: Stopping time of the generated time signals. t_end = 'Auto' derives t_end from the sampling of the S-parameter. The time signals start at t=0.

n: Number of calculated time samples. n = 'Auto' derives n from the sampling of the S-parameter.

Frequency Domain Filter frame

Use AR-filter results [3D Simulation only]: AR-filtered S-parameters are used.

No filter: The unfiltered S-parameters are used. This is equivalent to a band limited Dirac delta input signal.

CST Official Help | 3D common preloadedmacro common preloadedmacro tdr from time signals
Time Signal Processing / TDR from Time Signals

P ost-Processing: Tools > Result Templates

This result templates calculates time domain reflectometry (TDR) results time signals. Refer to the general introduction of the TDR computation for more theoretical details.

Specify Port/Mode [3D Simulation] or Specify Task/Port [Circuits & Systems] frame

Defines the time signals used for the TDR calculation.

Gaussian Pulse options frame

Shift T_0 (TDR) to 50% (Pulse): The origin of the time delay axis is shifted to the time where the integrate pulse has risen to 50% of its maximal amplitude.

Calculate Reflection Factor: The template calculates the reflection factor.

Rise time given by Gaussian Pulse frame

Displays properties of the used Gaussian pulse excitation :

Fmax: Frequency where the pulse spectrum has dropped to 10% of its peak amplitude

Trise: Time delay between the 10% and 90% amplitude of the integrated Gaussian pulse

Spatial resolution frame

Displays the spatial resolution of the used pulse.

CST Official Help | 3D special theory special theory time domain reflectometry tdr
Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR)

TDR computation (Time Domain Reflection) is well known from measurement, where TDR is the only possibility to "look into a structure" and locate mismatches. Typically TDR is applied to TEM structures such as connectors or IC packages designed to have minimum return loss. The quality of the calculated TDR result chiefly depends on the used excitation signal.

From transmission line theory, the transmission coefficient $T_{k,k+1}$ and the reflection coefficient $\Gamma_{k,k+1}$ at an impedance discontinuity from $Z_k$ to $Z_{k+1}$ are \begin{eqnarray} T_{k,k+1} &=& \frac{2Z_{k+1}}{Z_{k+1}+Z_{k}} \\ \Gamma_{k,k+1} &=& \frac{Z_{k+1}-Z_{k}}{Z_{k+1}+Z_{k}}\\ o_k &=& \Gamma_{k,k+1} i \end{eqnarray} where the input signal $i$ leaves space $k$ and the reflection $o_k$ is returned into $k$.
